Now CSS. Add sidebar scroll properties to base, sidebar-close/scrim base, mobile changes, dark. Also adjust mobile menu.

Base modifications:
`.sidebar{...overflow-y:auto;overflow-x:hidden;overscroll-behavior:contain;scrollbar-width:thin;scrollbar-color:#d8dfec transparent;}` Add `scrollbar-gutter: stable`? Could add but may shift content; use `scrollbar-gutter: stable` optional no.

Also `max-height:100dvh` maybe.

Add base rules near end (before dark appended) or after theme block. New rules appended at end ensures overrides. But media max700 earlier rules must be overridden by later media max700. We'll append blocks at end.

Need `.sidebar-close` hidden base; in mobile show. Scrim.

Mobile:
```
@media(max-width:700px){
 .sidebar{width:min(82vw,304px);padding:20px 16px calc(18px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom));border-right:1px solid #e1e6ef;box-shadow:18px 0 45px rgba(28,40,68,.16);visibility:hidden;overscroll-behavior:contain;}
 .sidebar.open{visibility:visible}
```
But existing `.sidebar` has `transform:translateX(-100%);transition:transform .25s;width:260px;box-shadow...` from earlier media. Our later `.sidebar` rule overrides width/shadow but transform/transition remain. Need set `transition:transform .3s cubic-bezier(.22,.8,.3,1),visibility .3s;` and visibility hidden. When closed, visibility hidden after transition? `transition:... visibility .3s` will delay hide, okay. Or use `visibility:hidden` immediately; then no closing animation visible (slide out invisible). Better keep transition of visibility with delay on close, but simple: `.sidebar{visibility:hidden;transition:transform .3s ease,visibility .3s}`; `.sidebar.open{visibility:visible}`. Visibility interpolates discretely at end for hidden; with transition duration, the hide happens at end of 0.3s, allowing slide-out. Good.
- z-index 10? Base sidebar z5, scrim maybe 9? Need layering with topbar. Set `.sidebar{z-index:12}` on mobile, scrim 11? But modal z15, toast z20, so sidebar 12 < modal 15. Topbar z4 under scrim. Good. Scrim z11. But on desktop scrim none. Sidebar desktop z5. In mobile override z-index 12.
- Scrim `position:fixed;inset:0;background:rgba(16,25,43,.44);backdrop-filter:blur(2px);z-index:11;display:block;opacity:0;visibility:hidden;pointer-events:none;transition:...` Base display none outside mobile. Define base `.sidebar-scrim{display:none}` then inside media display block. `.sidebar-scrim.open{opacity:1;visibility:visible;pointer-events:auto}`. But specificity `.sidebar-scrim.open` after. Fine.
- `body.sidebar-open{overflow:hidden}` within media. But `body[style overflow hidden]` from modal not conflict.
- menu button: existing media rule:
`.mobile-menu{display:grid;gap:4px;width:29px;height:29px;place-content:center;background:#fff;border:1px solid #e9edf4;border-radius:8px}`. Override with width 36 height 36, border-radius 11, gap 5; span width 15 height 1.8; add transitions; open transforms into X:
```
.mobile-menu span{transition:transform .22s,opacity .22s}
.mobile-menu[aria-expanded=true] span:first-child{transform:translateY(3.5px) rotate(45deg)}
.mobile-menu[aria-expanded=true] span:last-child{transform:translateY(-3.5px) rotate(-45deg)}

## Objective
- Improve the existing Paperly PDF workspace, first removing the top-right user avatar and adding preference-aware light/dark mode and playful hover animations, then expanding the PDF split tool with multiple range-selection methods.

## Requirements
- For splitting PDFs, offer a table, the previous manual range input, and visual page selection from the PDF contents.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Table is the default split mode, with an initial `1–1` row.
- Adjacent pages selected in the visual picker combine into a range; multiple output PDFs are downloaded as a ZIP.
- Theme follows system preference unless the user has saved a manual choice.

## Work State
### Completed
- Removed the top-right avatar and added a light/dark theme toggle, persistence, system preference support, hover-hop animations, and reduced-motion support.
- Added split modes: editable range table, manual comma-separated ranges, and PDF page-thumbnail picker.
- Added live range/output summaries, validation, selection controls, staged thumbnail loading, responsive styling, and dark theme styling.
- Tested table, manual, and visual selection in-browser using an 8-page PDF; verified generated PDF page counts and ZIP contents.
- `node --check app.js`, `git diff --check`, and browser console checks passed.

### Active
- Changes are complete but remain uncommitted.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. If further work is requested, inspect current changes in `app.js`, `index.html`, and `styles.css`.
2. Commit changes only if requested.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: theme handling, split tool UI/state, PDF previews and splitting logic.
- `index.html`: top-right actions; user avatar removed.
- `styles.css`: animations, theme variants, split modes and responsive layouts.

## Important Context
- Current git status had uncommitted modifications to `app.js`, `index.html`, and `styles.css`.
- Browser tests verified table ranges `1–2` and `3–5`, picker ranges `2–3` and `6`, and manual input `1-2, 8`; output PDF page counts matched selections.

## Objective
- Improve the existing Paperly PDF workspace’s responsive layout and sidebar, then animate the hero’s PDF illustration and remove the top-right Help button.

## Requirements
- User requested: “Tambahkan animasi pada logo ilustrasi file PDF [Dokumen rapi, pikiran pun lega.] dengan menghadirkan animasi berupa logo file PDF yang bergerak layaknya ditulis dan animasi pendukung lainnya yang dinamis. Hapus pula fitur bantuan *Tanda Tanya* pada sebelah kanan atas.”
- Earlier requirements: responsive mobile and desktop UI; sidebar scrolls on mobile and dismisses when tapping the app area behind it; remove the “Ruang kerja / semua alat 8” and profile “P / Ruang pribadi / Gratis selamanya” elements.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Sidebar dismissal uses a blurred/dimmed backdrop tap and Escape; no X button.
- “Semua alat” remains, without the count badge.
- Sidebar and topbar were redesigned with a mobile Paperly brand, desktop local-processing status, shortcut cards, and privacy card.
- Earlier split-PDF work remains in the project: table, manual ranges, and visual page selection.

## Work State
### Completed
- Responsive sidebar/topbar redesign, internal sidebar scrolling, backdrop dismissal, keyboard Escape handling, and removal of the requested sidebar profile and count.
- Verified responsive widths from 320px to 1440px, light/dark styling, sidebar scroll and dismissal, modal access, and no console errors.
- Existing split-PDF modes and theme support were previously implemented and browser-tested.
### Active
- Add dynamic “written” animation to the hero PDF illustration and supporting animations.
- Remove the top-right Help button (“Tanda Tanya”) and its related UI/handler.
### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the hero illustration markup/styles and implement a reduced-motion-aware PDF drawing/writing animation with complementary motion.
2. Remove the Help button and its event handler, then adjust topbar spacing.
3. Verify in browser at mobile and desktop sizes, check light/dark and reduced-motion behavior, and run syntax/diff checks.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: hero illustration, topbar, sidebar markup.
- `styles.css`: hero artwork animations, responsive breakpoints, theme variants.
- `app.js`: Help button handler, theme and sidebar interactions.

## Important Context
- Changes to `app.js`, `index.html`, and `styles.css` are uncommitted.
- Prior checks passed: `node --check app.js`, `git diff --check`, and browser console checks.

## Objective
- Improve Paperly’s responsive PDF workspace/sidebar and animate the hero PDF illustration; remove the top-right Help button.

## Requirements
- Keep the interface responsive on mobile and desktop.
- On mobile, allow sidebar scrolling and dismiss it by tapping the app area behind it.
- Remove the sidebar “Ruang kerja / semua alat 8” and profile elements; retain “Semua alat” without its count.
- Animate the hero PDF illustration as if being written, with dynamic supporting motion.
- Remove the top-right Help button (“Tanda Tanya”).

## Decisions
- Sidebar closes by tapping the dimmed backdrop or pressing Escape; no close button.
- Use reduced-motion-aware animation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Responsive sidebar/topbar redesign, sidebar scrolling, backdrop dismissal, and Escape handling.
- Removed the requested sidebar profile and tool-count elements.
- Removed the Help button markup from `index.html`.

### Active
- Implement the hero illustration animation.
- Remove the Help button event handler and related unused CSS, then verify the changes.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add reduced-motion-aware drawing/writing and supporting animations to the hero PDF illustration.
2. Remove the `helpButton` event handler in `app.js` and clean up obsolete Help-button CSS.
3. Verify mobile/desktop layouts, light/dark themes, reduced-motion behavior, and run syntax/diff checks.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Hero illustration and topbar; Help button markup has been removed.
- `styles.css`: Hero artwork styles and animation rules.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve Paperly’s responsive PDF workspace/sidebar and animate the hero PDF illustration; remove the top-right Help button.

## Requirements
- Keep the interface responsive on mobile and desktop.
- On mobile, allow sidebar scrolling and dismiss it by tapping the app area behind it.
- Remove sidebar “Ruang kerja / semua alat 8” and profile elements; retain “Semua alat” without its count.
- Animate the hero PDF illustration as if being written, with dynamic supporting motion.
- Remove the top-right Help button (“Tanda Tanya”).

## Decisions
- Close the mobile sidebar by tapping the dimmed backdrop or pressing Escape; no close button.
- Respect reduced-motion preferences for animations.

## Work State
### Completed
- Responsive sidebar/topbar redesign, sidebar scrolling, backdrop dismissal, and Escape handling.
- Removed the requested sidebar profile and tool-count elements.
- Removed the Help button markup from `index.html`.

### Active
- Add reduced-motion-aware writing/drawing and supporting animations to the hero PDF illustration.
- Remove the stale `helpButton` event handler in `app.js` and obsolete Help-button CSS.
- Verify changes.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement the hero illustration animation in `styles.css`.
2. Remove the `helpButton` event handler from `app.js` and clean up obsolete Help-button styles.
3. Verify mobile/desktop layouts, light/dark themes, reduced-motion behavior, and run syntax/diff checks.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Hero illustration and topbar; Help button markup removed.
- `styles.css`: Hero artwork styles and animation rules.
- `app.js`: Stale handler still references the removed `helpButton`.

## Important Context
- Changes to `app.js`, `index.html`, and `styles.css` are uncommitted.
- Existing split-PDF modes and theme support were previously implemented and browser-tested.
- Earlier checks passed, but the latest markup change has not yet been verified.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve Paperly’s responsive PDF workspace/sidebar and animate the hero PDF illustration; remove the top-right Help button.

## Requirements
- Keep the interface responsive on mobile and desktop.
- On mobile, allow sidebar scrolling and dismiss it by tapping the app area behind it.
- Remove sidebar “Ruang kerja / semua alat 8” and profile elements; retain “Semua alat” without its count.
- Animate the hero PDF illustration as if being written, with dynamic supporting motion.
- Remove the top-right Help button (“Tanda Tanya”).

## Decisions
- Close the mobile sidebar by tapping the dimmed backdrop or pressing Escape; no close button.
- Respect reduced-motion preferences for animations.

## Work State
### Completed
- Redesigned responsive sidebar/topbar, added mobile sidebar scrolling, backdrop dismissal, and Escape handling.
- Removed the requested sidebar count/profile elements and Help button markup.
- Added reduced-motion-aware writing/drawing and supporting animations to the hero illustration.
- Removed the stale Help-button event handler and obsolete Help-button CSS rules.

### Active
- Re-run syntax and diff checks after the latest CSS cleanup; browser/layout verification remains pending.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run `git diff --check` and `node --check app.js`.
2. Verify mobile/desktop layouts, light/dark themes, and reduced-motion behavior in a browser.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Sidebar, topbar, and hero illustration markup.
- `styles.css`: Responsive layouts, themes, and hero animation rules.
- `app.js`: Mobile sidebar behavior and event handlers.

## Important Context
- Changes to `app.js`, `index.html`, and `styles.css` are uncommitted.
- Syntax, structural CSS, and diff checks passed before the latest removal of obsolete Help-button CSS; no browser verification has been performed since the animation changes.

import { createRequire } from 'node:module'
import { readFileSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join } from 'node:path'
const runtime = join(process.env.HOME, '.local/share/omgithub-playwright')
const require = createRequire(join(runtime, 'package.json'))
const { chromium } = require('playwright')
const config = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(runtime, 'linux.json'), 'utf8'))
const lib = require(process.cwd() + '/vendor/pdf-lib.min.js')
const PDF = 'file:///tmp/opencode/assets/sample.pdf'
let passed = 0
const ok = (label, cond) => { if (!cond) throw new Error('GAGAL: ' + label); console.log('✓', label); passed++ }

const browser = await chromium.launch({ ...config.browser.launchOptions, headless: true })
const errors = []
try {
  const ctx = await browser.newContext({ viewport: { width: 1440, height: 900 } })
  const page = await ctx.newPage()
  page.on('pageerror', e => errors.push('pageerror: ' + e.message))
  page.on('response', r => { if (r.status() >= 400 && r.url().includes('127.0.0.1:8765')) errors.push(`HTTP ${r.status()}: ${r.url()}`) })
  await page.goto('http://127.0.0.1:8765', { waitUntil: 'load' })

  ok('8 kartu alat dirender', await page.locator('#toolsGrid .tool-card').count() === 8)
  await page.fill('#toolSearch', 'pisah')
  ok('pencarian memfilter ke 1 kartu', await page.locator('#toolsGrid .tool-card').count() === 1)
  await page.fill('#toolSearch', '')
  ok('mengosongkan pencarian kembali ke 8', await page.locator('#toolsGrid .tool-card').count() === 8)

  // Modal open/close
  await page.click('[data-tool="split"]')
  ok('modal terbuka dengan judul Pisah PDF', (await page.textContent('#modalTitle')).trim() === 'Pisah PDF')
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape')
  ok('Escape menutup modal', await page.locator('#toolModal').evaluate(el => !el.classList.contains('open')))

  // Gambar ke PDF
  await page.locator('#toolsSection').scrollIntoViewIfNeeded()
  await page.screenshot({ path: '/tmp/opencode/assets/img.png', clip: { x: 300, y: 300, width: 400, height: 300 } })
  await page.click('[data-tool="images"]')
  await page.setInputFiles('#fileInput', '/tmp/opencode/assets/img.png')
  ok('baris file gambar muncul', (await page.locator('#fileRows .file-row').count()) === 1)
  let dl = page.waitForEvent('download')
  await page.click('#modalAction')
  dl = await dl
  const imgPdf = '/tmp/opencode/assets/out-images.pdf'
  await dl.saveAs(imgPdf)
  ok('unduhan gambar→PDF dibuat (' + Math.round(statSync(imgPdf).size / 1024) + ' KB)', readFileSync(imgPdf).slice(0, 5).toString() === '%PDF-')
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape')

  // Gabungkan
  await page.click('[data-tool="merge"]')
  await page.setInputFiles('#fileInput', [PDF, PDF])
  ok('dua file terdaftar', (await page.locator('#fileRows .file-row').count()) === 2)
  dl = page.waitForEvent('download')
  await page.click('#modalAction')
  await (await dl).saveAs('/tmp/opencode/assets/out-merge.pdf')
  ok('PDF gabungan valid', readFileSync('/tmp/opencode/assets/out-merge.pdf').slice(0, 5).toString() === '%PDF-')
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape')

  // Pisah
  await page.click('[data-tool="split"]')
  await page.setInputFiles('#fileInput', PDF)
  await page.waitForFunction(() => document.querySelector('.picker-status')?.textContent.includes('3'))
  ok('split membaca 3 halaman', true)
  dl = page.waitForEvent('download')
  await page.click('#modalAction')
  await (await dl).saveAs('/tmp/opencode/assets/out-split.pdf')
  const splitDoc = await lib.PDFDocument.load(readFileSync('/tmp/opencode/assets/out-split.pdf'))
  ok('hasil pisah berisi 1 halaman', splitDoc.getPageCount() === 1)
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape')

  // Tanda air + jalur error
  await page.click('[data-tool="watermark"]')
  dl = page.waitForEvent('download')
  await page.click('#modalAction')
  await (await dl).catch(() => null)
  ok('validasi teks kosong menampilkan error', await page.locator('#modalError').evaluate(el => el.classList.contains('show')))
  await page.fill('#watermarkText', 'DRAF')
  dl = page.waitForEvent('download')
  await page.click('#modalAction')
  await (await dl).saveAs('/tmp/opencode/assets/out-watermark.pdf')
  ok('tanda air menghasilkan PDF', readFileSync('/tmp/opencode/assets/out-watermark.pdf').slice(0, 5).toString() === '%PDF-')
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape')

  // Kompres
  await page.click('[data-tool="compress"]')
  await page.setInputFiles('#fileInput', PDF)
  dl = page.waitForEvent('download', { timeout: 30000 })
  await page.click('#modalAction')
  await (await dl).saveAs('/tmp/opencode/assets/out-compress.pdf')
  ok('kompres menghasilkan unduhan', true)
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape')

  // Tema gelap
  await page.click('#themeToggle')
  ok('tema gelap aktif', await page.locator('body').getAttribute('data-theme') === 'dark')
  await page.screenshot({ path: '/tmp/opencode/paperly-capture/dark-desktop.png' })
  await page.click('#themeToggle')

  // Mobile
  await page.setViewportSize({ width: 390, height: 844 })
  ok('menu mobile tersembunyi di desktop?', await page.locator('#mobileMenu').evaluate(el => getComputedStyle(el).display !== 'none'))
  await page.click('#mobileMenu')
  ok('sidebar terbuka', await page.locator('#sidebar').evaluate(el => el.classList.contains('open')))
  ok('main content inert saat sidebar terbuka', await page.locator('.main-content').evaluate(el => el.hasAttribute('inert')))
  await page.screenshot({ path: '/tmp/opencode/paperly-capture/mobile-sidebar.png' })
  await page.click('#sidebarScrim', { position: { x: 370, y: 400 }, force: true })
  ok('ketuk backdrop menutup sidebar', await page.locator('#sidebar').evaluate(el => !el.classList.contains('open')))
  await page.click('#mobileMenu')
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape')
  ok('Escape menutup sidebar', await page.locator('#sidebar').evaluate(el => !el.classList.contains('open')))
  await ctx.close()

  // Reduced motion
  const rctx = await browser.newContext({ viewport: { width: 1440, height: 900 }, reducedMotion: 'reduce' })
  const rpage = await rctx.newPage()
  await rpage.goto('http://127.0.0.1:8765', { waitUntil: 'load' })
  ok('animasi hero berhenti saat reduced motion', await rpage.locator('.page-front').evaluate(el => getComputedStyle(el).animationName === 'none'))
  await rctx.close()

  ok('tanpa error halaman / respons gagal', errors.length === 0)
} finally { await browser.close() }
console.log(`\nSEMUA UJI LOLOS: ${passed} pemeriksaan`)

## [GitHub - cantoo-scribe/pdf-lib: Create and modify PDF documents in any JavaScript environment · GitHub](https://github.com/cantoo-scribe/pdf-lib)

* LICENSE.md
* README.md
* eslint.config.js
* jest.config.js
* package.json
* pdf_specification.pdf
* rollup.config.mjs
* tsconfig.json
* tslint.json
* yarn.lock

README.md

Forked by Cantoo

@cantoo/pdf-lib is an actively maintained fork of Hopding/pdf-lib . We keep the original API and docs, and ship the features below that upstream does not (or no longer) provide. Install with:
npm install @cantoo/pdf-lib
# or
yarn add @cantoo/pdf-lib
We maintain this project for our own product needs and cannot guarantee support for every issue outside that roadmap — but contributions that fit the library are welcome.

Benefits vs original pdf-lib

Drawing & content
* Full SVG drawing ( page.drawSvg / embedSvg ) — not just drawSvgPath : shapes, text, transforms, viewBox cropping, blend modes, rounded rects, CSS colors via culori
* PDFPage.extractContents() — pull typed assets (text, images, approximate vector graphics as SVG) out of page content streams

...

* convertToPDFA() — PDF/A-1/2/3 structural pieces (OutputIntent + sRGB ICC, /ID , XMP synced with Info)
* embedFacturX() — Factur-X / ZUGFeRD PDF/A-3 hybrid invoices
Security & crypto
* PDFDocument.encrypt() — AES-256 revision 6 by default; AES-128 / RC4 via algorithm (RC4 needs allowWeakCryptography )
* Decrypt PDFs whose crypt filters are indirect objects
* No crypto-js : in-tree AES/RC4/MD5/SHA-256 + Web Crypto getRandomValues
Fonts & layers
* First-class @cantoo/fontkit support (types, default export, UMD); still compatible with upstream fontkit / @pdf-lib/fontkit
* postscriptName to pick a face from .ttc / .dfont collections
* Optional content (PDF layers) — getOptionalContentGroups() / setOptionalContentGroupVisibility()
Packaging & deps
* Vendored @cantoo/upng and @cantoo/standard-fonts (also as @cantoo/pdf-lib/upng and @cantoo/pdf-lib/standard-fonts )
* Compression via fflate instead of pako (modular TS UPNG with Photopea quantize / framize / lossy cnum )

...

Help and Discussion

Discussions is the best place to chat with us, ask questions, and learn more about pdf-lib!
See also MAINTAINERSHIP.md#communication and MAINTAINERSHIP.md#discord .

Encryption Handling

pdf-lib does support encrypted documents.
If you do not have a password yet, you can load the document without decrypting it to check whether it is encrypted:
// Load without decrypting (encrypted content will not be readable):
const doc = await PDFDocument.load(content, { ignoreEncryption: true });
const isEncrypted = doc.isEncrypted;
// If isEncrypted is true, ask the user for the password.
To decrypt and load the document, pass the password. ignoreEncryption is not required:
// Load and decrypt an encrypted document:
const doc = await PDFDocument.load(content, { password: 'The password' });
An empty password is valid for some PDFs. Pass it explicitly — do not omit the option or treat '' as "no password":
const doc = await PDFDocument.load(content, { password: '' });
If the password is wrong, PDFDocument.load throws an error.
To encrypt a document, call encrypt() before saving. The default cipher is AES-256 (ISO 32000-2 revision 6). The document's PDF version is not used to pick the algorithm — pass algorithm if you must target an older viewer. RC4 is refused unless you also set allowWeakCryptography: true :
const doc = await PDFDocument.create();
doc.addPage().drawText('Hello!');

doc.encrypt({
  userPassword: 'user-pw',
  ownerPassword: 'owner-pw',
  permissions: { printing: 'highResolution' },
  // algorithm: 'AES-128', // optional; default is 'AES-256'
});

const bytes = await doc.save();
Requirement: encrypt() needs the Web Crypto API ( crypto.getRandomValues ) to generate secure random keys, salts, and IVs. That is available in modern browsers, Node >= 18 , Deno, and Bun. On older Node versions, or in React Native without a polyfill such as react-native-get-random-values , encrypt() throws. No other part of pdf-lib requires it — loading, decrypting, and saving unencrypted documents all work without it.

Contributing

We welcome contributions from the open source community! If you are interested in contributing to pdf-lib , please take a look at the CONTRIBUTING.md file. It contains information to help you get pdf-lib setup and running on your machine. (We try to make this as simple and fast as possible! 🚀)

Maintainership

Check out MAINTAINERSHIP.md for details on how this repo is maintained and how we use issues , PRs , and discussions .

## [Password-protecting PDFs in JavaScript: what the encryption hides and what it doesn't - DEV Community](https://dev.to/dummyipsum/password-protecting-pdfs-in-javascript-what-the-encryption-hides-and-what-it-doesnt-5089)
Published: 2026-11-06T00:00:00.000Z

# webdev # javascript # security # pdf
Adding a password to a PDF in JavaScript takes three lines. Knowing what that password actually protects takes a bit longer. I built a browser-only PDF protect tool and ran a few experiments along the way with @cantoo/pdf-lib (a maintained pdf-lib fork that supports encryption) and pdfjs-dist . Here is what I learned.

 The basic version

import { PDFDocument } from ' @cantoo/pdf-lib ' ; const doc = await PDFDocument . load ( inputBytes ); doc . encrypt ({ userPassword : password , ownerPassword : password , algorithm : ' AES-256 ' , }); const protectedBytes = await doc . save ({ useObjectStreams : true });
It runs in the browser, so the file never leaves the user's device. That is the main reason to do it client-side: people protect PDFs because the content is sensitive, and uploading it to a server first defeats the purpose.

 1. There are two passwords, and only one of them encrypts

A PDF has a user password (needed to open the file) and an owner password (needed to change the permissions: printing, copying, editing).
The user password is the one that matters. If you leave it empty and set only an owner password, the document still opens for everyone. I tested it: a file with userPassword: '' and an owner password opened in pdf.js with no password at all and returned the full page text.
The permission flags are just a number in the file ( /P ). The viewer decides whether to respect them. Firefox's PDF viewer (pdf.js) ignores them by default: its enablePermissions option is false . And removing them takes two lines:
const doc = await PDFDocument . load ( ownerOnlyBytes , { password : '' }); const unrestricted = await doc . save (); // no /Encrypt dictionary any more
So "can't print, can't copy" is a polite request, not security. If the content is confidential, set a user password.

 2. Omitting permissions denies everything

In @cantoo/pdf-lib , if you set passwords but no permissions object, every permission is off. My test file ended up with /P -3904 , which decodes to: no printing, no copying, no editing, no form filling, not even the copy-for-accessibility flag.
That's a safe default for the library, but probably not what you want when the goal is "only people with the password can open it". Once someone types the password, they usually should be able to print the document. Be explicit:
doc . encrypt ({ userPassword : password , ownerPassword : password , algorithm : ' AES-256 ' , permissions : { printing : ' highResolution ' , modifying : true , copying : true , annotating : true , fillingForms : true , contentAccessibility : true , documentAssembly : true , }, });

 3. Encryption doesn't hide the document's structure

PDF encryption works on strings and streams: page content, images, fonts, metadata values. The object structure around them stays readable.
I encrypted a three-page test file with the title "Salary review Q3" and the author "Jane Smith", then searched the raw bytes:
* Searched for | Without object streams | With object streams
* Jane Smith | not found | not found
* /Author key | found | not found
* /Type /Page | found | found
* /Count 3 | found | found
* /MediaBox | found | found
The metadata values and the page text are encrypted either way. But anyone with the file can still see that it has three pages and what size they are, without the password. useObjectStreams: true hides more of the structure (the Info dictionary keys moved into an encrypted object stream), but the page tree stayed visible in my test.
Usually that is fine. If the page count itself is sensitive, PDF encryption is the wrong tool, and you should encrypt the whole file (a password-protected 7z, age, GPG).

 4. The cipher matters less than the password

@cantoo/pdf-lib supports four algorithms:
* RC4-40 and RC4-128 : broken. The library refuses them unless you pass allowWeakCryptography: true .
* AES-128 : the /V 4 handler from PDF 1.6.
* AES-256 : the /V 5 /R 6 handler, the library's default and the one ISO 32000-2 (PDF 2.0) recommends. In a PDF 1.7 file it is declared as an Adobe extension.
Both AES options are fine. The weak point is the password. The encryption key is derived from it, and neither PDF handler uses a slow, memory-hard function like Argon2 or scrypt. Whoever has the file can try passwords offline as fast as their hardware allows, with no rate limit and no lockout. A six-letter password will not survive that, so ask for a long one, ideally several random words.
And send the password through a different channel than the file. A password in the same email as the attachment protects nothing.

 5. Verify the output before you hand it over

A file that "should" be encrypted is not the same as a file that is. Before offering the download, I reopen the result with pdf.js three ways:
import * as pdfjs from ' pdfjs-dist ' ; async function tryOpen ( bytes , password ) { try { const pdf = await pdfjs . getDocument ({ data : bytes . slice (), password }). promise ; return pdf . numPages ; } catch  ( error ) { if  ( error . name === ' PasswordException ' ) return null ; throw error ; } } const withoutPassword = await tryOpen ( protectedBytes ); const wrongPassword = await tryOpen ( protectedBytes , password + ' x ' ); const rightPassword = await tryOpen ( protectedBytes , password ); const ok = withoutPassword === null && wrongPassword === null && rightPassword === originalPageCount ;
Two details: pass a copy ( bytes.slice() ), because pdf.js may transfer the buffer to its worker and leave you holding an empty one. And check error.name , so a damaged file isn't reported as "password works".

no password -> PasswordException: No password given

I wanted a "password protect this PDF" tool. pdf-lib doesn't do encryption. Not a flag I missed — it isn't implemented.
@cantoo/pdf-lib is a fork that adds it, with the same API:
await doc . encrypt ({ userPassword : pw , ownerPassword : pw });
The reverse direction is more interesting. PDFs have two kinds of password:
* Owner password — restrictions on printing, copying, editing. This is a flag the viewer is politely asked to respect. Load with ignoreEncryption: true , save again, restrictions gone. It was never security.
* User password — actual encryption. The file content is genuinely encrypted and without the password there is nothing to recover.
So the unlock tool removes the first and cannot touch the second, and the FAQ says exactly that. I'd rather explain the limit than have someone assume we're a cracking service.

import { createRequire } from 'node:module'
import { readFileSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join } from 'node:path'
const runtime = join(process.env.HOME, '.local/share/omgithub-playwright')
const require = createRequire(join(runtime, 'package.json'))
const { chromium } = require('playwright')
const config = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(runtime, 'linux.json'), 'utf8'))
const Cantoo = require(process.cwd() + '/vendor/pdf-lib-cantoo.min.js')
const fs = { readFileSync }
const A = '/tmp/opencode/assets'
const PDF = A + '/sample.pdf'
const PNG = A + '/img.png'
let passed = 0
const ok = (label, cond) => { if (!cond) throw new Error('GAGAL: ' + label); console.log('✓', label); passed++ }
const head = f => fs.readFileSync(f).slice(0, 5).toString()

const browser = await chromium.launch({ ...config.browser.launchOptions, headless: true })
const errors = []
try {
  const ctx = await browser.newContext({ viewport: { width: 1440, height: 900 } })
  const page = await ctx.newPage()
  page.on('pageerror', e => errors.push('pageerror: ' + e.message))
  page.on('console', m => { if (m.type() === 'error') errors.push('console: ' + m.text()) })
  await page.goto('http://127.0.0.1:8765', { waitUntil: 'load' })

  /* ===== REGRESI FITUR LAMA ===== */
  ok('12 kartu alat dirender', await page.locator('#toolsGrid .tool-card').count() === 12)
  await page.fill('#toolSearch', 'pisah')
  ok('pencarian memfilter', await page.locator('#toolsGrid .tool-card').count() === 1)
  await page.fill('#toolSearch', '')
  ok('pencarian kosong → 12', await page.locator('#toolsGrid .tool-card').count() === 12)
  await page.click('[data-tool="split"]')
  ok('modal Pisah terbuka', (await page.textContent('#modalTitle')).trim() === 'Pisah PDF')
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape')
  ok('Escape menutup modal', await page.locator('#toolModal').evaluate(el => !el.classList.contains('open')))

  await page.screenshot({ path: '/tmp/opencode/paperly-capture/grid-12.jpg', quality: 60, type: 'jpeg' })

  // Gambar ke PDF
  await page.locator('#toolsSection').scrollIntoViewIfNeeded()
  await page.click('[data-tool="images"]')
  await page.setInputFiles('#fileInput', PNG)
  let dl = page.waitForEvent('download')
  await page.click('#modalAction')
  await (await dl).saveAs(A + '/out-images.pdf')
  ok('gambar→PDF valid', head(A + '/out-images.pdf') === '%PDF-')
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape')

  // Gabungkan
  await page.click('[data-tool="merge"]')
  await page.setInputFiles('#fileInput', [PDF, PDF])
  dl = page.waitForEvent('download')
  await page.click('#modalAction')
  await (await dl).saveAs(A + '/out-merge.pdf')
  ok('gabungan 6 halaman', (await Cantoo.PDFDocument.load(fs.readFileSync(A + '/out-merge.pdf'))).getPageCount() === 6)
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape')

  // Pisah
  await page.click('[data-tool="split"]')
  await page.setInputFiles('#fileInput', PDF)
  await page.waitForFunction(() => document.querySelector('[data-fill-all]'))
  dl = page.waitForEvent('download')
  await page.click('#modalAction')
  await (await dl).saveAs(A + '/out-split.pdf')
  ok('pisah → 1 halaman', (await Cantoo.PDFDocument.load(fs.readFileSync(A + '/out-split.pdf'))).getPageCount() === 1)
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape')

  // Tanda air

## Objective
- Improve Paperly’s responsive PDF workspace and hero illustration, then add OCR, PDF password encryption/unlocking, and visual PDF editing.
- Complete due diligence testing and publish the changes to GitHub `main`.

## Requirements
- Keep the interface responsive on mobile and desktop; mobile sidebar scrolls and dismisses by backdrop tap or Escape.
- Remove sidebar workspace/count and profile elements, keep “Semua alat” without its count, and remove the top-right Help button.
- Animate the hero PDF as if being written, with supporting motion that respects reduced-motion preferences.
- Add OCR, password-protect, unlock, and edit-PDF features; test new and existing features.

## Decisions
- Use Tesseract.js for OCR, with English and Indonesian options; OCR runs locally after the engine is downloaded.
- Use `@cantoo/pdf-lib` for PDF encryption and unlocking.
- PDF editing adds text, images, and freehand drawing as overlays while preserving original pages.
- Preserve the `main` versions of three `.omgithub` runtime files during merge conflicts because the workflow references them.

## Work State
### Completed
- Responsive sidebar, hero animations, requested UI removals, and all four PDF features implemented.
- Due diligence completed: 35 Playwright checks passed, covering new and existing tools, mobile behavior, themes, reduced motion, and PDF output validation.
- Changes committed and pushed to `opencode/43768378554`; merged and pushed to `origin/main` as merge commit `ad2a62c`.

- `app.js`: PDF tools, OCR, encryption/unlocking, editor, and sidebar behavior.
- `index.html`: Tool cards, app structure, and vendor script loading.
- `styles.css`: Responsive layouts, hero animation, and editor styling.
- `vendor/pdf-lib-cantoo.min.js`: Vendored encryption-capable PDF library.
- `vendor/PDF-LIB-CANTOO-LICENSE.md`: License for the vendored library.

## 1. Pembuat PDF → halaman tulis khusus
- Klik kartu **Pembuat PDF** kini membuka **halaman layar penuh**, bukan modal: bilah atas dengan tombol **← Kembali**, judul "Tulis dokumen baru", label jumlah halaman, dan tombol **Buat PDF** (spinner + progress bar gradien saat merakit)
- Kanvas A4 lebih lega (max 760px, center), toolbar **sticky** di atas saat menulis panjang, fokus otomatis ke kanvas saat dibuka
- Konten **bertahan** saat halaman ditutup dan dibuka lagi; ditutup lewat tombol Kembali atau Escape; scroll body terkunci selama menulis

## 2. Alat dikelompokkan dalam groupbox
Halaman utama kini modular dalam **4 groupbox**, masing-masing dengan judul, deskripsi, dan lencana jumlah alat:
- **Tulis & Sunting** (2 alat) — Pembuat PDF, Edit PDF
- **Kelola Halaman** (5 alat) — Pisah, Gabungkan, Ekstrak, Putar, Nomor
- **Optimasi & Keamanan** (4 alat) — Kompres, Enkripsi, Buka kunci, Tanda air
- **Ubah Format** (4 alat) — PDF→Word, PDF→PPT, OCR, Gambar→PDF

## Objective
- Continue developing Paperly’s PDF workspace by adding a blank-page PDF writer and PDF-to-Word/PPTX conversion.
- Move the writer into a dedicated writing page and organize related tools on the homepage into modular group boxes.

## Requirements
- Provide a blank-page PDF creator with comprehensive Word-like editing features.
- Convert PDFs to Word (`.docx`) and PowerPoint (`.pptx`).
- Open the PDF creator on a dedicated page for more comfortable editing.
- Group related homepage tools into tidy, modular group boxes.
- Run due diligence before committing the new features.

## Decisions
- The proposed writer uses a browser-based rich-text editor and exports to PDF.
- The proposed Word and PowerPoint exports are generated as OOXML packages; PDF-to-PPTX slides are page images.

## Work State
### Completed
- Existing responsive workspace, PDF tools, OCR, encryption/unlocking, PDF editor, progress indicators, and batch processing are implemented and merged into `main`.
- The progress/OCR/batch update passed 44 checks and was merged as `77fada1`.

### Active
- Integrate the PDF writer and PDF-to-Office conversion features.
- Make the writer a dedicated page and organize related tools into homepage group boxes.
- Test the new features and existing functionality before committing.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the current `app.js`, `index.html`, and `styles.css`, then integrate the drafted writer/conversion code with the requested dedicated-page and grouped-homepage UX.
2. Run browser and output-validation tests, fix issues, and only then commit.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Existing PDF tools and likely integration point for writer/conversion behavior.
- `index.html`: Homepage tool cards and app structure; update for tool groups and dedicated writer page.
- `styles.css`: Responsive styling for tool groups, writing page, and editor.
- `/tmp/opencode/office-block.txt`: Draft writer and PDF-to-Office implementation; inspect before reuse.

## Important Context
- The last confirmed `main` merge is `77fada1`; no integration, tests, or commit for the newer writer/conversion or dedicated-page/grouping requests are confirmed.
- Earlier assistant work drafted code in `/tmp/opencode/office-block.txt`, but did not show it being integrated into repository files.

10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.

- Complete Paperly’s PDF workspace with a blank-page writer, PDF-to-Office conversions, PDF/A and JPG conversions, and a tidier homepage layout; test before committing.

- Test new and existing functionality before committing.

- Use a browser-based rich-text editor for writing and PDF export.
- Generate Office exports as OOXML packages; PDF-to-PPTX slides are page images.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Tool definitions, writer, Office export, and PDF-processing paths.
- `index.html`: App structure and writer page markup.
- `styles.css`: Tool-group layout and writer styling.

- No PDF/A or PDF-to-JPG tools were found in the inspected `app.js` definitions.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete Paperly’s PDF workspace with a blank-page writer, PDF-to-Office conversions, PDF/A and JPG conversions, and a tidier homepage layout; test before committing.

## Requirements
- Provide Word-like writing and PDF export.
- Convert PDFs to `.docx` and `.pptx`.
- Add PDF-to-PDF/A and PDF-to-JPG conversions.
- Organize related homepage tools into modular groups.
- Test new and existing functionality before committing.

## Decisions
- Use a browser-based rich-text editor for writing and PDF export.
- Generate Office exports as OOXML packages; PDF-to-PPTX slides are page images.

## Work State
### Completed
- Confirmed the writer, PDF export, PDF-to-Word, PDF-to-PowerPoint, and homepage tool groups are implemented.
- Confirmed PDF/A and PDF-to-JPG tools were missing from `app.js`.

### Active
- Implement PDF/A and PDF-to-JPG conversions and place them in appropriate homepage groups.
- Review writer and Office conversion behavior for gaps; test functionality before committing.

### Blocked
- No current blocker. An earlier draft file `/tmp/opencode/office-block.txt` was missing; work has not depended on it.

## Next Move
1. Add PDF/A and PDF-to-JPG tool definitions, processing paths, and homepage group placement.
2. Review writer, Office conversion, and homepage grouping behavior.
3. Run browser and output-validation tests, fix issues, and only then commit.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Tool definitions, groups, writer/Office exports, and PDF processing paths.
- `index.html`: Homepage and writer page markup.
- `styles.css`: Homepage tool-group layout and writer styling.
- `vendor/`: Local PDF libraries, PDF.js, and fflate.

## Important Context
- The working tree was clean at the latest status check; no changes, tests, or commit are confirmed.
- A 456-byte sRGB ICC profile was downloaded to `/tmp/opencode/srgb.icc` from `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/saucecontrol/Compact-ICC-Profiles/master/profiles/sRGB-v2-micro.icc`; the repository reports the source project license as CC0-1.0 via its GitHub API metadata. No repository files were changed.

## Objective
- Complete Paperly’s PDF workspace by adding PDF/A and PDF-to-JPG conversions, reviewing existing writer and Office conversion tools, and testing before committing.

## Requirements
- Provide Word-like writing and PDF export.
- Convert PDFs to `.docx` and `.pptx`.
- Add PDF-to-PDF/A and PDF-to-JPG conversions.
- Organize related homepage tools into modular groups.
- Test new and existing functionality before committing.

## Decisions
- Use a browser-based rich-text editor for writing and PDF export.
- Generate Office exports as OOXML packages; PDF-to-PPTX slides are page images.

## Work State
### Completed
- Confirmed the writer, PDF export, PDF-to-Word, PDF-to-PowerPoint, and homepage tool groups are implemented.
- Confirmed PDF/A and PDF-to-JPG tools are missing from `app.js`.
- Inspected existing tool definitions, conversion paths, and writer/Office implementation; no repository changes were made.

### Active
- Implement PDF/A and PDF-to-JPG conversion paths and add them to appropriate homepage groups.
- Test the new conversions and existing functionality, fix issues, and commit only after validation.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add PDF/A and PDF-to-JPG tool definitions, processing paths, and homepage group placement.
2. Review writer, Office conversions, and homepage grouping for gaps.
3. Run browser and output-validation tests, fix issues, then commit.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Tool definitions, homepage groups, writer/Office exports, and PDF processing paths.
- `index.html`: Homepage and writer page markup.
- `styles.css`: Homepage tool-group layout and writer styling.
- `vendor/`: Local PDF libraries, PDF.js, and fflate.

## Important Context
- Working tree was clean at the latest status check; no changes, tests, or commit are confirmed.

- `/tmp/opencode/office-block.txt` was missing earlier; work has not depended on it.

3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete Paperly’s PDF workspace by adding PDF/A and PDF-to-JPG conversions, reviewing existing writing and Office conversion tools, testing functionality, and committing after validation.

## Requirements
- Provide Word-like writing and PDF export.
- Convert PDFs to `.docx` and `.pptx`.
- Add PDF-to-PDF/A and PDF-to-JPG conversions.
- Organize related homepage tools into modular groups.
- Test new and existing functionality before committing.

## Decisions
- Use a browser-based rich-text editor for writing and PDF export.
- Generate Office exports as OOXML packages; PDF-to-PPTX slides are page images.
- PDF/A implementation should embed an sRGB profile and add PDF output-intent and metadata entries.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected existing writer, PDF export, Office conversion tools, homepage groups, and PDF library primitives.
- Experimentally verified PDF-lib can save and reload a PDF with output-intent and metadata entries.

### Active
- Implement and register PDF/A and PDF-to-JPG tools and place them in appropriate homepage groups.
- Review writer, Office conversions, and homepage grouping for gaps.
- Run browser and output-validation tests, fix issues, then commit.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Implement and register PDF/A and PDF-to-JPG tools and add them to homepage groups.
2. Review writer, Office conversions, and homepage grouping for gaps.
3. Run browser and output-validation tests, fix issues, then commit.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Tool definitions, homepage groups, conversion handlers, and PDF processing; has an uncommitted import change for PDF-lib low-level dictionary and stream construction.
- `index.html`: Homepage and writer page markup.
- `styles.css`: Homepage tool-group layout and writer styling.
- `vendor/srgb.icc`: Added sRGB profile for PDF/A output.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; no tests or commit have been made.
- Existing homepage groups place `toWord`, `toPpt`, `ocr`, and `images` under `konversi`; PDF/A and JPG tools are not yet registered.
- PDF-to-PPTX renders each PDF page to a JPEG image on a slide; PDF-to-Word extracts text by line into OOXML.
- `vendor/srgb.icc` is 456 bytes, sourced from `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/saucecontrol/Compact-ICC-Profiles/master/profiles/sRGB-v2-micro.icc` (CC0-1.0).

## Objective
- Complete Paperly’s PDF workspace with PDF/A and PDF-to-JPG conversions, review the writer and Office conversions, test functionality, and commit after validation.

## Requirements
- Provide Word-like writing and PDF export; convert PDFs to `.docx` and `.pptx`.
- Add PDF-to-PDF/A and PDF-to-JPG conversions; organize related homepage tools into groups.
- Test new and existing functionality before committing.

## Decisions
- Use a browser-based rich-text editor for writing and PDF export.
- Generate Office exports as OOXML packages; PDF-to-PPTX slides are page images.
- PDF/A output is rasterized to JPG-backed pages, then given an sRGB output intent and PDF/A-2b metadata; conformance still needs external validation.

- Commit changes after validation.

- No browser tests or output-validation tests have been run.

## Next Move
1. Run browser-based checks for PDF-to-JPG single/multiple-page outputs and PDF/A output.

3. Review writer, Word/PowerPoint exports, and homepage groups; test and fix issues.

## Relevant Files

- `index.html`: Homepage and writer page markup.
- `styles.css`: Homepage tool-group layout and writer styling.
- `vendor/srgb.icc`: sRGB profile used by PDF/A generation.

- `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` passed; no browser test, Office export review, or commit has occurred.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete Paperly’s PDF workspace by adding PDF/A and PDF-to-JPG conversions, reviewing the writer and Office conversions, testing functionality, and committing validated changes.

## Requirements
- Provide Word-like writing with PDF export; convert PDFs to `.docx` and `.pptx`.
- Add PDF-to-PDF/A and PDF-to-JPG conversions; organize related homepage tools into groups.
- Test new and existing functionality before committing.

## Decisions
- Use a browser-based rich-text editor for writing and PDF export.
- Generate Office exports as OOXML packages; PDF-to-PPTX slides are page images.
- PDF/A output rasterizes pages to JPG, adds an sRGB output intent and PDF/A-2b metadata, and retains a notice that validation is needed.

## Work State
### Completed
- Registered PDF/A and PDF-to-JPG tools and added them to the homepage conversion group.
- Implemented PDF-to-JPG rendering with direct download for one page and ZIP packaging for multiple pages.
- Updated PDF/A generation to rasterize pages, add an sRGB profile and output intent, and set PDF/A metadata.
- Added progress reporting for PDF/A rendering.
- `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Test PDF-to-JPG and PDF/A conversions, and review/test the writer, Word/PowerPoint exports, and homepage grouping.
- Commit changes after validation.

### Blocked
- PDF/A conformance remains unvalidated; `veraPDF`, `qpdf`, and `mutool` are unavailable.
- Browser-based and generated-output tests have not run; Selenium, Playwright, and Puppeteer packages are unavailable. Chromium and ChromeDriver are installed.
- A local HTTP server attempt on port 8765 failed because the port was already in use.

## Next Move
1. Run browser-based checks for PDF-to-JPG single- and multi-page outputs and PDF/A output.
2. Validate PDF/A conformance with an external validator; adjust implementation or claims as needed.
3. Review and test the writer, Word/PowerPoint exports, and homepage groups; fix issues found.
4. Re-run `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check`, then commit the validated changes.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Tool definitions, homepage groups, PDF/A/JPG helpers, conversion processing, writer, and Office export code.
- `index.html`: Homepage and writer page markup.
- `styles.css`: Homepage tool-group layout and writer styling.
- `vendor/srgb.icc`: sRGB profile used by PDF/A generation.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted: `app.js` is modified and `vendor/srgb.icc` is untracked.
- PDF/A generation rasterizes source pages, so text and vector content are not preserved as searchable or editable content.
- `vendor/srgb.icc` is a 456-byte ICC profile.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete Paperly’s PDF workspace with PDF/A and PDF-to-JPG conversions, review the writer and Office conversions, test functionality, and commit validated changes.

## Requirements
- Provide Word-like writing with PDF export; convert PDFs to `.docx` and `.pptx`.
- Add PDF-to-PDF/A and PDF-to-JPG conversions and organize related homepage tools into groups.
- Test new and existing functionality before committing.

## Decisions
- Use a browser-based rich-text editor for writing and PDF export.
- Generate Office exports as OOXML packages; PDF-to-PPTX slides are page images.
- PDF/A output rasterizes pages to JPG, adds an sRGB output intent and PDF/A-2b metadata, and retains a notice that validation is needed.

## Work State
### Completed
- Registered PDF/A and PDF-to-JPG tools and added them to the homepage conversion group.
- Implemented PDF-to-JPG rendering with direct download for one page and ZIP packaging for multiple pages.
- Updated PDF/A generation to rasterize pages, add an sRGB profile and output intent, and set PDF/A metadata.
- Tested both JPG download paths and PDF/A conversion in Chrome using generated sample PDFs.
- Tested writer PDF export and Word/PowerPoint exports; the DOCX/PPTX ZIP packages were valid and their XML parsed successfully.
- Verified `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` pass.

### Active
- Commit the validated, currently uncommitted changes.

### Blocked
- PDF/A conformance has not been externally validated; `veraPDF`, `qpdf`, and `mutool` are unavailable.

## Next Move
1. Run PDF/A through an external validator when available; the generated file’s metadata and output intent were inspected but that does not establish conformance.
2. Commit the changes after deciding whether external PDF/A validation is required before committing.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Tool definitions, homepage groups, PDF/A/JPG conversion code, writer, and Office export code.
- `vendor/srgb.icc`: sRGB profile used by PDF/A generation.
- `index.html`: Homepage and writer page markup.
- `styles.css`: Homepage tool-group layout and writer styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted: `app.js` is modified and `vendor/srgb.icc` is untracked.
- PDF/A generation rasterizes source pages, so text and vector content are not preserved as searchable or editable content.
- Browser tests produced a two-page JPG ZIP, a single-page JPG, a two-page PDF/A, a DOCX, a two-slide PPTX, and a writer PDF.

Colors available: lilac, mint, peach, blue, yellow, rose. Redact → rose fits well (security). Icon: add 'redact' icon. Now plan the implementation: ### A. Writer image/object insertion (doc builder) Enhancements to `initDocBuilder`: 1. Keep toolbar image button, but improve `docImageInput` handler: insert at caret, and make inserted image selectable + resizable. 2. Add drag-and-drop of image files onto doc pages, and paste of image data. 3. Selection: clicking an image adds class `doc-img-selected`; render a resize handle (span appended to a positioned wrapper? Simpler: images are block-level in contenteditable; wrap not allowed to break export code which reads `block.el` as IMG with getComputedStyle width). Handle: absolutely position handle relative to image via wrapper div would break `collectDocBlocks` (it would see div with children? The div would contain img → `el.querySelector('img')` matches, so div gets skipped as container... Actually collectDocBlocks skips elements that contain p/h1/etc/img/div children, so a wrapper div containing img would be skipped and the img itself still collected since querySelectorAll('...,img,...') finds img directly. OK either way.) Simpler approach: keep img as-is; add a selected outline via class and a floating resize handle appended to the page (absolutely positioned near img corner) while selected. That's fiddly. Alternative: use a fixed-position handle computed from getBoundingClientRect. Even simpler: while image selected, show a small inline toolbar (floating div in docBuilder) with width controls (25%, 50%, 75%, 100%, Hapus). That's clean, robust, and touch-friendly: no drag math. I'll do: click image → show `.doc-img-tools` floating bar near image with buttons: Kecilkan (−), Perbesar (+), Penuh, Hapus. Width adjustments set style.width as % of page width; export uses computed width so it carries over. Also Escape/Delete key removes selection. Blur when clicking elsewhere. 4. Drag&drop + paste images into pages: - 'paste' event on pages: check clipboardData.files/images → insert dataURL img at caret. - 'drop' on docPages: prevent default, read image files, insert at caret (focus page first). Also handle very large images: downscale to max 1400px wide canvas → JPEG/PNG dataURL to keep PDF size sane. I'll downscale to max 1600px and keep PNG if small? Simplify: draw to canvas max 1600px, export as PNG if original is png and small else JPEG 0.92. Just do canvas → toDataURL('image/jpeg',0.92) unless PNG with transparency? For simplicity keep original dataURL but downscale via canvas when naturalWidth>1600, output jpeg 0.9 for photos, png for png. I'll implement helper `readImageAsDataUrl(file)`. 5. Update docIsEmpty already checks img. Export: already handles img blocks. One issue: images inserted inline within a text paragraph: collectDocBlocks pushes img as block; runs skip it; fine. ### B. Redact tool New tool entry after 'unlock' maybe in Optimasi & Keamanan group: ids ['compress','protect','unlock','redact','watermark']. Tool def: {id:'redact',title:'Redact PDF',description:'Tutup informasi rahasia dengan aman.',detail:'Tandai area teks atau grafis yang sensitif, lalu halaman yang ditandai dirender ulang sebagai gambar sehingga konten di balik blok benar-benar hilang — tidak hanya ditutupi. Halaman tanpa tanda tetap asli.',icon:'redact',color:'rose',tag:'BARU',input:'pdf',action:'Buka redaksi'} modalFields: redact editor: ```
toolbar: [Kosongkan halaman] [Hapus terpilih] + hint "Seret di halaman untuk menandai area." stage: canvas #redactPageCanvas + #redactBoxes layer + empty msg footer: prev/next + page label + count label "2 blok di halaman ini"

But maybe keyboard Delete when modal open... skip, buttons exist. Apply (case 'redact' in processTool): - If total boxes 0 → throw 'Tandai minimal satu area...'. - Load source pdf-lib doc (for pages without boxes, copyPages). - For pages with boxes: render via pdf.js at scale 2 (cap 2200px), draw black rects, embed JPEG 0.92 into new doc with page size = base viewport size. - For pages without boxes: copy original. - New doc: strip existing metadata (don't copy doc info) — created fresh, so no original metadata carries over (copyPages copies page content, not doc info). Good. Also don't set title/producer (or set Producer 'Paperly'). Keep neutral. - Output name `${base}-redaksi.pdf`. Note: redacted page loses text layer — mention in modal note. Icon 'redact': `` with a filled black bar? Use: `` hmm redaction usually shown as black bar over text. I'll use ``. Fine. ### C. openTool wiring - `modal.classList.toggle('split-wide', ...||activeTool.id==='redact')` - `if(activeTool.id==='edit')initEditor();` add `if(activeTool.id==='redact')initRedact();` - renderFileRows: `if(activeTool.id==='edit')updateEditorFile()` add redact update. - processTool: add case 'redact'. ### D. Earlier session had chromedriver at 9515 running already (no need to start?). That was earlier conversation; environment may persist? Klik blok untuk memindah atau menghapus.':'Pilih file PDF untuk mulai menandai.'} function updateRedactFile(){...same pattern as editor...} function gotoRedactPage(p){...} function renderRedactPage(){...render page canvas, then renderRedactBoxes(), updateRedactChrome()} function updateRedactChrome(){page label, prev/next disabled, buttons disabled when no boxes, hint text with count} function renderRedactBoxes(){layer.innerHTML=''; for each box create div.redact-box with left/top/width/height % and handle span; click select...} function onRedactStagePointerDown(e){if(!redact.doc||e.target.closest('.redact-box'))return; start drawing preview; pointermove update; pointerup commit if size ok} function startRedactBoxDrag(e,box,el,mode){move or resize} function deleteRedactSelected(){} function clearRedactPage(){} async function applyRedaction(file,onPage){boxes=redact.boxes; if none throw; load pdf-lib doc via readPDF; create out; for i pages: list=boxes[i+1]||[]; if list.length: render page via redact.doc (pdf.js) getPage(i+1) base viewport scale2 cap; draw rects; jpeg 0.92; embed; page size base; else copied from source via copyPages indices; progress; return out.save({useObjectStreams:false})? In applyRedaction, use redact.doc if available; if null, create fresh pdfjs doc. Safer: create fresh pdfjs from file bytes — avoids state issues. That doubles memory but fine. For canvas render at scale s: rect = box.x*cw, box.y*ch etc. Output page: use base viewport w/h (same as original page size). messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend the existing Paperly PDF workspace with richer PDF writing and security tools, and test the app thoroughly to minimize errors.

## Requirements
- Allow users to insert image objects in the PDF writer.
- Add a Redact PDF tool to permanently remove selected confidential content.
- Add a Flatten PDF tool to make PDF content non-editable.

## Decisions
- Redaction rasterizes marked pages so the covered content is removed rather than merely hidden; unmarked pages are preserved.
- Flattening rasterizes all pages, preserving page dimensions but removing selectable text and merging form fields and annotations into page images.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added PDF/A and PDF-to-JPG tools; validated browser download paths and Office/writer exports. Commit: `97ddc98`.
- Added image insertion and editing controls in the PDF writer, plus Redact PDF with page navigation and movable/resizable redaction blocks. Commit: `52e62f6`.
- Added Flatten PDF with Standard and High quality options. Commit: `61d70d5`.
- Browser-tested Redact and Flatten outputs, including checks that redacted text is absent and flattened pages contain images but no extractable text.
- Reported clean syntax/diff checks and a clean working tree after the latest commit.

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- External PDF/A conformance validation remains unverified; `veraPDF`, `qpdf`, and `mutool` were unavailable during earlier testing.

## Next Move
1. If PDF/A conformance is required, validate generated output with an external validator when available.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Tool definitions, writer image insertion, redaction, flattening, and conversion logic.
- `index.html`: Homepage and PDF writer markup.
- `styles.css`: Writer, redaction, flattening, and tool-group styling.
- `vendor/srgb.icc`: sRGB profile used by PDF/A generation.

## Important Context
- PDF/A validation remains a stated limitation; its metadata and output intent were inspected but conformance was not established.
- Redacted pages and flattened PDFs are raster images; text on those pages is not searchable or selectable.

Because `img.scrollIntoView(...)` was called JUST BEFORE `selectDocImage` — with `behavior:'smooth'`... no.

OH WAIT. I see it! `docImgSelected.getBoundingClientRect()` — but the image is inside `.doc-page` which is inside `.doc-pages` scroller. During positionDocImageBar, r.width=120... 

Hmm — unless `docImgSelected` is null at that point? No.

Actually — look at the ORDER in selectDocImage: bar appended, docImgBar=bar, positionDocImageBar(). At that instant, the img... rect 120 wide. UNLESS the bar's offsetWidth is NaN/undefined? bw=docImgBar.offsetWidth — bar has CSS `.doc-img-bar` — check display; if display:none initially → offsetWidth=0 → then `Math.max(8, Math.min(window.innerWidth-bw-8, r.left))` fine — no hiding.

The hiding condition is ONLY `if(!r.width)`. r.width=120... yet it hid. So r.width was 0 during that call. How?

`docImgSelected` — global set to img BEFORE. getBoundingClientRect of img — 0?? The final check after insertion showed 120. Between? Both in same synchronous flow... 

AH WAIT — maybe `scrollIntoView` didn't finish, but that doesn't zero the width.

Hmm — could `img.getBoundingClientRect()` return 0 because at that moment the img's SRC hadn't LOADED yet?! A data: URL image inserted into DOM — decode is async! Until loaded, the img element has no intrinsic size → width 0 (it's not styled). YES — that's it. The data URL loads asynchronously; getBoundingClientRect right after insertion gives 0×0.

Fix: in `positionDocImageBar`, don't hide the bar just because rect is 0 at that instant; instead if width is 0, retry on next frame or on img load. Better: make selectDocImage robust:
- Position the bar on `img.onload` too (or reposition when rect changes).

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Extend the existing Paperly PDF workspace with PDF tools and richer PDF-writer features.
- Keep the implementation and browser-tested outputs reliable.

## Requirements
- PDF writer: insert editable, movable spreadsheet-like objects; manually set font size with a spinbox; upload custom fonts.
- Add Redact PDF and Flatten PDF tools.
- Redaction must permanently remove selected content; flattening must make content non-editable.

## Decisions
- Redaction rasterizes marked pages while preserving unmarked pages.
- Flattening rasterizes every page, preserving page dimensions while removing selectable text and merging fields and annotations into page images.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added PDF/A and PDF-to-JPG tools; commit `97ddc98`.
- Added writer image insertion and Redact PDF; commit `52e62f6`.
- Added Flatten PDF with Standard and High quality; commit `61d70d5`.
- Added spreadsheet/table objects, font-size spinbox, and custom TTF/OTF upload and embedding; commit `d8bb710`.
- Pushed `d8bb710` to GitHub branch `opencode/43785953808`.
- Browser-tested Redact and Flatten outputs; tested writer controls and spreadsheet editing/operations.

### Active
- (none)

### Blocked
- Pull request creation was denied by repository settings: “GitHub Actions is not permitted to create or approve pull requests.”
- External PDF/A conformance remains unverified; `veraPDF`, `qpdf`, and `mutool` were unavailable during earlier testing.

## Next Move
1. If integration is wanted, create a PR from `opencode/43785953808` to `main` at https://github.com/Hattaakim/PDF-Tools-Ai-Project/pull/new/opencode/43785953808, or push directly to `main` with authorization.
2. If PDF/A conformance is required, validate generated output with an external validator.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: PDF tools, writer controls, spreadsheet objects, and export logic.

<subagent sessionID="ses_e17fd384effevcnjYXYw212l1h" state="completed">
## Findings in `app.js`

### 1. Confirmed: table and page-picker split modes use 1-based page numbers as 0-based copy indices

The PDF controls display pages starting at 1, but `PDFDocument.copyPages` expects zero-based page indices.

- In table mode, `currentSplitRanges()` builds IDs with `ids.push(n)` at **`app.js:75`**.
- In picker mode, it builds IDs with `r.start+i` at **`app.js:75`**. The picker groups user-facing page numbers in `selectionRanges()` at **`app.js:73`**.
- Split passes those IDs directly to `copyPages` at **`app.js:276`**.

```js
// app.js:75 — table mode
for(let n=a;n<=b;n++)ids.push(n);

// app.js:75 — picker mode
ids:Array.from({length:r.end-r.start+1},(_,i)=>r.start+i)

// app.js:276
copied=await piece.copyPages(doc,ranges[i].ids)
```

**Impact:** selecting page 1 copies page 2; selecting the document’s last page requests an out-of-range index. A one-page document cannot be split through these modes, and “select all” in the picker includes the invalid index `total`.

**Recommendation:** convert the user-facing number to a copy index in both branches: table IDs should use `n-1`, and picker IDs should use `r.start-1+i`. Add output-level tests for page 1, the last page, a one-page document, and select-all.

### 2. Manual split and extraction intentionally have different comma semantics

`parsePages()` at **`app.js:85`** parses 1-based single pages and ascending ranges, supports `-` and `–`, validates bounds, converts to zero-based indices, and removes duplicates while preserving first-seen order:

```js
if(a<1||b<a||b>total) ...
for(let n=a;n<=b;n++)
  if(!pages.includes(n-1))pages.push(n-1)
```

Extraction passes the complete field to that parser and creates one output PDF at **`app.js:267`**:

```js
ids=parsePages(document.getElementById('rangeField').value,doc.getPageCount())
```

Manual split instead separates on commas first, then parses each nonempty part independently at **`app.js:75`**. Each part becomes a separate output PDF; split outputs are assembled and downloaded at **`app.js:276`**.

For example, `1,3-4` in extraction yields one PDF containing pages 1, 3, and 4, in that order. In manual split it yields two PDFs. Overlapping manual split ranges therefore produce separate outputs containing the overlapping pages, while extraction deduplicates overlaps in its single output.

**Recommendation:** document and test this distinction, including ordering, overlaps, and duplicate requests. Also test empty comma segments: manual split filters them out, whereas `parsePages()` rejects an empty token—so inputs such as a trailing comma are handled differently.

### 3. Table-mode inputs can silently truncate decimals

At **`app.js:75`**, table values are parsed with `parseInt`:

```js
const a=parseInt(row.start),b=parseInt(row.end)
```

A numeric value such as `2.5` can therefore be interpreted as page 2 instead of rejected. The table inputs are `type="number"` at **`app.js:69`**, but the code reads their values directly rather than checking that they are integers.

**Recommendation:** validate that each nonempty value represents an integer before converting it, and add tests for decimal input, blank rows, and incomplete rows. The manual parser already rejects decimal tokens through its format check.

## Targeted regression tests

- **Index conversion:** In table and picker modes, selecting page 1 yields the source’s first page; selecting the final page works; selecting all pages yields the original page count. Include a one-page PDF.
- **Parser boundaries and format:** Test page 1, page `total`, out-of-range pages, descending ranges, malformed tokens, whitespace, hyphen/en dash, and trailing commas.
- **Ordering and overlap:** Verify extraction preserves first-requested order while deduplicating overlaps; verify split keeps manual/table range order and produces separate files for overlapping ranges.
- **Table validation:** Verify decimals are rejected rather than truncated, and that blank/incomplete rows behave as intended.

All relevant code is in **`/home/runner/work/PDF-Tools-Ai-Project/PDF-Tools-Ai-Project/app.js`**. No files were modified.

<skill_content name="gauntlet-loop">
# Skill: gauntlet-loop

# Gauntlet Loop

The user gives a goal. You give back ONE short prompt they can paste into a fresh agent session.

You are not doing the work. You are writing the prompt that makes another agent grind on the work until it beats a real reference.

## Flow

1. **Read the goal.** One line restatement in your head, not on screen.
2. **Set the bar.** If the user supplied a reference, use it. If not, offer **2 or 3 candidate bars**, one line each, and stop. Wait for their pick. Do not write the prompt yet.
3. **Write the prompt.** One block, paste-ready, no preamble, no headings inside it, no narration after it.
4. **Offer to run it.** One flat line under the prompt: "I can run this here." Not a question.

If they say run it, you become the lead agent and follow the prompt you just wrote.

## The bar is the whole trick

Everything else in a gauntlet loop is scaffolding. The loop only produces quality if the thing it compares against is real.

A bar has to pass three tests:

- **Named.** A specific thing, not a category. "Stripe's pricing page" works. "Award-winning SaaS sites" does not.
- **Fetchable.** The critic can actually get it - screenshot the live page, read the published piece, run the binary, open the repo, watch the footage. If the agent cannot obtain it, it will hallucinate the comparison.
- **Comparable.** Both can sit side by side and a judge can pick one. If you cannot imagine the A/B, it is not a bar.

Bars by goal type:

| Goal | Bar that works |
|---|---|
| Website, app, UI | The live site of a specific best-in-class product, screenshotted at the same viewport |
| Game, 3D, visual | Real footage or screenshots from a named shipped title |
| Writing | A specific published piece by a named author or publication, same length and format |
| Code, tooling | A named repo's implementation, plus its benchmark or test suite as the measurable half |
| Research, analysis | A named analyst report or a paper's methods section, judged on rigour and coverage |
| Deck, doc, deliverable | A real artifact from a firm known for it, same page count |

When you propose bars, prefer the hardest one the agent can genuinely reach. A bar that is too easy makes the loop exit on round one.

If the goal has a measurable half (load time, token cost, benchmark score, word count, pass rate), name it alongside the reference. Taste plus a number beats taste alone.

## Prompt template

Adapt the wording every time. Fill the brackets, keep it short, keep the last line.

```
Build [GOAL].

The bar is [BAR]. Get the real thing first and compare against it directly, not against a description of it.

Break this into the smallest pieces that can be improved and judged on their own. For each piece, fan out a builder and a separate critic with fresh context. The critic inspects the actual output, puts it next to the bar blind with the labels stripped, says which one is better, and names the single biggest remaining gap. Then it goes back to the builder.

The critic should be a harsh critic. Praise is not useful. If ours does not win, it keeps going.

/loop on each piece until the critic picks ours blind. Do not stop before that.

Keep a live progress page updating as the work evolves so I can watch it.

Fan out subagents and ultracode.
```

Rules for what you fill in:

- Bake the bar in as a concrete, fetchable thing. URL, product name, repo, title.
- Add a budget or cost ceiling line **only if the user named one**. No default cap.
- Add tool names only if the goal needs them (image or video generation, a browser, a deploy target).
- Everything else stays out. No architecture, no file layout, no decomposition, no round count, no stack choice unless the user demanded it. The agent decides those, and it decides better than a spec written before the work started.

## Length and voice

Short. Around 120 to 180 words. If the prompt needs a heading to stay readable, it is too long.

Plain sentences. No bullet lists inside the prompt. It should read like someone telling an agent what perfect looks like and refusing to accept less.

## Portability

`/loop` and `ultracode` are Claude Code features. `/loop` reruns the prompt on an interval or lets the model pace itself. `ultracode` opts the turn into multi-agent orchestration.

For any other agent, swap the last two lines for: "Keep looping until the critic picks ours. Run the builders and critics as parallel subagents." The structure carries over unchanged.

## Two filled examples

**Visual goal.** User: "landing page for my running brand, athletic, green and dark, has to feel alive."

Bars offered: A) Nike's current running campaign page B) On Running's homepage C) Gymshark's product landing page. User picks A.

```
Build a landing page for a running brand. Athletic, peak performance, green and dark, energetic, aimed at a young healthy audience. It needs to be interactive and visually unmistakable.

The bar is Nike's current running campaign page. Screenshot it at desktop and mobile and compare against those directly, not against a description of them.

Break this into the smallest pieces that can be improved and judged on their own - hero, motion, type, colour, imagery, interaction, mobile. For each piece, fan out a builder and a separate critic with fresh context. The critic opens the real page in a browser, puts our screenshot next to Nike's blind with the labels stripped, says which is better, and names the single biggest remaining gap. Then it goes back to the builder.

The critic should be a harsh critic. Praise is not useful. If ours does not win, it keeps going.

/loop on each piece until the critic picks ours blind. Do not stop before that.

Keep a live progress page updating as the work evolves so I can watch it.

Fan out subagents and ultracode.
```

**Non-visual goal.** User: "a 2000-word explainer on vector databases for non-engineers."

Bars offered: A) a specific Stripe engineering blog explainer B) a named Julia Evans post C) the Wikipedia article plus a comprehension test. User picks B.

```
Write a 2000-word explainer on vector databases for readers who are smart but not engineers.

The bar is Julia Evans' writing on hard technical topics. Pull three of her actual posts and compare against them directly, not against a description of her style.

Break this into the smallest pieces that can be judged on their own - the opening, each explanation, the diagrams, the analogies, the ending. For each piece, fan out a writer and a separate critic with fresh context. The critic reads ours and hers blind with the bylines stripped, says which one a non-engineer would understand faster, and names the single biggest remaining gap. Then it goes back to the writer.

The critic should be a harsh critic. Praise is not useful. If ours does not win, it keeps going.

/loop on each piece until the critic picks ours blind. Do not stop before that.

Keep a live progress page updating as the work evolves so I can watch it.

Fan out subagents and ultracode.
```

## What breaks a gauntlet loop

- **A vague bar.** The critic invents a comparison and approves everything. Most common failure by far.
- **The builder judging its own work.** The critic must be a separate agent with fresh context. It should not know how hard the builder tried.
- **A soft critic.** Say "harsh" in the prompt and give it a binary job: which one is better, A or B. Scores out of 10 drift upward every round.
- **Named exit after N rounds.** The exit is winning the comparison, or the user stopping the run. Never a round count.
- **Over-specifying.** Every extra instruction is one fewer decision the agent makes with its own judgment. Minimal wins.
